question: The September 2025 guidelines on Anganwadi–School co-location emphasise which key component of child development?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Early Childhood Care and Education**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE)** focuses on the holistic development of children during their formative years (0-6 years), including cognitive, emotional, social, and physical aspects.
 
• The **September 2025 guidelines on Anganwadi–School co-location** aim to integrate Anganwadi centers with schools to ensure a seamless transition and continuity in education for children.
 
• By co-locating Anganwadi centers and schools, the guidelines emphasize creating a strong foundation for **school readiness**, ensuring children are adequately prepared for formal schooling.
 
• The guidelines also focus on enhancing access to **quality early childhood education** for marginalized communities, addressing disparities in educational opportunities.
 
• This initiative aligns with the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**, which highlights ECCE as a critical factor in achieving universal foundational literacy and numeracy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Importance of Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE):**

 
 
• ECCE lays the foundation for lifelong learning, fostering **critical thinking**, creativity, and socio-emotional skills.
 
• Research highlights that the brain develops most rapidly during the first six years of life, making these years crucial for **cognitive and emotional growth**.
 
• Quality ECCE programs have been shown to improve **academic performance** and reduce dropout rates in later years.
 
• ECCE also plays a role in breaking the cycle of **poverty**, providing equitable opportunities to children from economically disadvantaged backgrounds.
 
 
 
• **Anganwadi Centers:**
 
 
• Established under the **Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme**, Anganwadi centers provide a range of services, including health, nutrition, and education, for children up to 6 years old.
 
• These centers focus on improving maternal and child health, ensuring adequate nutrition, and preparing children for school.
 
• There are approximately **1.37 million Anganwadi centers** across India as of 2023.
 
 
 
• **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020:**
 
 
• The NEP 2020 emphasizes universal access to ECCE by 2030 through the establishment of Anganwadi centers and pre-primary schools.
 
• It recommends the integration of **play-based and activity-based learning** approaches to enhance foundational literacy and numeracy.
 
• The policy also highlights teacher training and capacity building to improve the quality of ECCE programs.
 
 
 
• **Additional Government Initiatives for ECCE:**
 
 
• **Poshan Abhiyaan:** Focuses on improving nutritional outcomes for children, pregnant women, and lactating mothers.
 
• **Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan:** Supports school readiness and ECCE through infrastructure development and capacity building.
 
• **Saksham Anganwadi Scheme:** Aims to upgrade Anganwadi centers into modern resource hubs for ECCE and maternal health services.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Teachers and Caregivers:**

 
 
• Teachers and Anganwadi workers are trained to deliver **age-appropriate educational content** and foster a nurturing environment.
 
• Continuous professional development programs ensure the adoption of **best practices** in ECCE.
 
 
 
• **Global Perspective on ECCE:**
 
 
• Countries like Finland and Sweden have successfully implemented robust ECCE systems, emphasizing play-based learning and holistic development.
 
• UNICEF advocates for universal access to ECCE as a strategy to achieve **Sustainable Development Goal 4** (Quality Education).
 
 
 
• **Challenges in ECCE Implementation:**
 
 
• Lack of infrastructure and resources in remote areas limits access to quality ECCE programs.
 
• Ensuring equitable access for marginalized communities remains a key challenge.
